Amazon Aurora MySQL with automatic storage scaling 🎯 Trigger mapping: "Expected to grow continuously" + "16 TiB current" + "automatic scaling" + "pay-per-use" directly maps to Aurora's automatic scaling up to 128 TiB with usage-based billing, unlike RDS's 64 TiB limit. RDS MySQL: Limited to 64 TiB maximum DynamoDB: NoSQL, not MySQL compatible Redshift: Data warehouse, not OLTP database

A solutions architect proposes using Lambda@Edge functions to replace EC2-based Ruby on Rails applications for weather simulation processing. Why is this problematic? A. Lambda@Edge has a 15-minute execution time limit unsuitable for long simulations B. Lambda@Edge is designed for CloudFront content customization, not compute-intensive applications C. Lambda@Edge cannot connect to databases in private subnets D. Lambda@Edge only supports Python and Node.js, not Ruby ✅ B. Lambda@Edge is designed for CloudFront content customization, not compute-intensive applications Lambda@Edge is architected specifically for lightweight request/response processing at CloudFront edge locations. It's not designed for heavy computational workloads like weather simulations that require substantial processing power and time. 🎯 Better approach: Use ECS with Fargate or EC2 Auto Scaling for containerized or traditional compute workloads that need consistent processing power and flexible runtime environments.

A company is launching an online shopping website with security against man-in-the-middle attacks including DNS spoofing, HTTPS spoofing, and SSL hijacking. The architecture uses AWS Fargate with an Application Load Balancer and CloudFront for content delivery. They need the MOST secure configuration following industry best practices. Which configuration provides the MOST secure access to the website? A. Register domain on Route 53. Host DNS root servers on EC2 with BIND for DNSSEC. Generate ACM certificate and configure ALB HTTPS listener. Use SNI and HTTP to HTTPS redirection on CloudFront. B. Register domain on Route 53. Use third-party DNS provider with customer-managed DNSSEC keys. Import third-party SSL certificate to ACM. Configure ALB HTTPS listener. Use SNI and HTTP to HTTPS redirection on CloudFront. C. Use Route 53 for registration. Use third-party DNS with DNSSEC and customer-managed keys. Generate ACM certificate and configure ALB HTTPS listener. Use SNI and HTTP to HTTPS redirection on CloudFront. D. Register domain on Route 53 and enable DNSSEC validation for public hosted zones. Generate ACM certificate and configure ALB HTTPS listener. Use SNI and HTTP to HTTPS redirection on CloudFront. ✅ D. Use Route 53 with native DNSSEC validation and ACM-generated certificates 🎯 Why correct: Route 53 now natively supports DNSSEC signing for public hosted zones, eliminating the need for third-party DNS providers or custom EC2 DNS servers. ACM provides free, automatically-renewed SSL certificates that integrate seamlessly with ALB. ⚠️ A. EC2-hosted BIND DNS servers This was a workaround solution before Route 53 supported DNSSEC natively. Running custom DNS servers on EC2 adds unnecessary complexity, management overhead, and potential security vulnerabilities compared to the fully managed Route 53 DNSSEC service. ⚠️ B. Third-party DNS with imported certificates Unnecessarily complex and costly. Route 53 supports DNSSEC natively, so there's no need for third-party DNS providers. Additionally, importing third-party certificates to ACM when ACM can generate free certificates adds unnecessary expense and manual certificate management. ⚠️ C. Third-party DNS service While technically possible, this introduces dependency on external providers when Route 53 already provides native DNSSEC support. This adds complexity without security benefits and may introduce additional points of failure in the DNS resolution chain.

Which statement about Route 53 DNSSEC implementation is correct? A. Route 53 manages both zone-signing keys and key-signing keys automatically without customer involvement. B. Route 53 manages the zone-signing key while customers manage the key-signing key in AWS KMS. C. Customers must manage both zone-signing keys and key-signing keys in separate AWS KMS instances. D. Route 53 DNSSEC only works with third-party certificate authorities for key management. ✅ B. Route 53 manages zone-signing keys, customers manage key-signing keys in KMS 🎯 Key Management Split: Route 53 automatically handles zone-signing key management for operational simplicity, while customers retain control over key-signing keys through AWS KMS for security compliance. This provides the right balance of automation and control for enterprise security requirements. ⚠️ A. Fully automatic: Incorrect - customers maintain control over key-signing keys for security compliance. ⚠️ C. Customer manages both: Wrong - Route 53 manages zone-signing keys to reduce operational burden. ⚠️ D. Third-party CAs required: False - Route 53 DNSSEC works independently of certificate authorities.

When should you choose ACM-generated certificates over imported third-party certificates? A. When you need certificates with custom key sizes or extended validation. B. When you want automatic renewal, cost savings, and seamless AWS integration. C. When you require certificates that work with non-AWS load balancers. D. When you need certificates for internal/private domain names. ✅ B. For automatic renewal, cost savings, and seamless AWS integration ACM-Generated Certificates • Free of charge • Automatic renewal • Native AWS integration • Simplified management • Works with ALB, CloudFront, API Gateway Imported Third-Party Certificates • Manual renewal required • Additional cost • Custom validation types (EV, OV) • Works outside AWS • Custom key sizes/algorithms 🎯 Decision rule: Choose ACM-generated for standard AWS deployments needing cost-effective, automatically-managed certificates. Choose imported certificates when you need extended validation, custom attributes, or use outside AWS.

A company needs to prevent DNS spoofing attacks and ensure DNS responses haven't been tampered with in transit for their public-facing e-commerce website. Which AWS service feature best addresses this requirement? A. CloudFront signed URLs with custom origins B. Route 53 DNSSEC validation and signing C. WAF rate limiting rules with IP reputation D. VPC Flow Logs with DNS query monitoring ✅ B. Route 53 DNSSEC validation and signing 🎯 DNS Security: DNSSEC cryptographically signs DNS records to provide data origin authentication and integrity verification. Route 53 DNSSEC validation ensures DNS responses haven't been tampered with, directly preventing DNS spoofing attacks. ⚠️ A. CloudFront signed URLs: Protects content access but doesn't address DNS-level attacks. ⚠️ C. WAF rate limiting: Protects against application-layer attacks, not DNS spoofing. ⚠️ D. VPC Flow Logs: Provides monitoring but no active protection against DNS attacks.

An e-commerce site requires: protection against SSL hijacking , automatic certificate renewal , HTTP to HTTPS redirection , and SNI support for multiple domains . Which combination meets ALL requirements? A. ACM certificate on ALB + CloudFront with custom SSL certificate B. Third-party certificate on ALB + CloudFront signed URLs C. ACM certificate on ALB + CloudFront with SNI and HTTP redirect D. Self-signed certificate on ALB + CloudFront with dedicated IP ✅ C. ACM certificate on ALB + CloudFront with SNI and HTTP redirect 🎯 Requirements mapping: ACM provides automatic renewal and SSL hijacking protection through valid certificates. ALB terminates SSL securely. CloudFront SNI supports multiple domains cost-effectively while HTTP redirect ensures secure connections. This combination addresses all security and operational requirements. ⚠️ A. Custom SSL certificate: Doesn't specify automatic renewal or HTTP redirect capabilities. ⚠️ B. Third-party + signed URLs: Requires manual renewal, signed URLs don't provide HTTP redirect. ⚠️ D. Self-signed certificate: Provides no protection against SSL hijacking, causes browser warnings.

A multi-national tech company has multiple VPCs with peering connections. They need to launch a central database server accessible via database.tutorialsdojo.com . The server must be resolvable and accessible only within the associated VPCs for internal applications. Which solution should the architect implement? A. Set up a public hosted zone with tutorialsdojo.com, create A record for database.tutorialsdojo.com, enable DNS hostnames and support B. Set up a private hosted zone with tutorialsdojo.com, create A record for database.tutorialsdojo.com, enable DNS hostnames and support C. Set up a public hosted zone with tutorialsdojo.com, create CNAME record for database.tutorialsdojo.com, disable DNS hostnames and support D. Set up a private hosted zone with tutorialsdojo.com, create A record mapping to Elastic IP, enable DNS hostnames, disable DNS support ✅ B. Set up a private hosted zone with tutorialsdojo.com, create A record for database.tutorialsdojo.com, enable DNS hostnames and support 🎯 Why correct: A private hosted zone ensures DNS resolution only within associated VPCs, meeting the internal-only requirement. Both enableDnsHostnames and enableDnsSupport must be true for proper DNS functionality within VPCs. ⚠️ A. Public hosted zone approach A public hosted zone would make the database resolvable from the internet, violating the requirement that it should only be accessible within associated VPCs. Public zones are for internet-facing resources. ⚠️ C. Public zone with disabled DNS Not only does this use a public hosted zone (wrong for internal-only access), but disabling DNS hostnames and support would prevent proper DNS resolution within the VPCs entirely. ⚠️ D. Elastic IP with disabled DNS support While it correctly uses a private hosted zone, disabling DNS support breaks DNS resolution functionality. Additionally, Elastic IPs are public IPv4 addresses reachable from the internet, violating the internal-only requirement.

When should you choose a private hosted zone over a public hosted zone in Route 53? A. When you need DNS resolution for resources accessible from the internet B. When you need DNS resolution only within specific VPCs for internal resources C. When you want to reduce DNS query costs for high-traffic websites D. When you need faster DNS propagation times globally ✅ B. When you need DNS resolution only within specific VPCs for internal resources Private Hosted Zone • DNS resolution within associated VPCs only • Internal resources and applications • Enhanced security for internal services • Requires VPC association Public Hosted Zone • DNS resolution from the internet • Public-facing websites and services • Global DNS propagation • No VPC association needed 🎯 Decision rule: Choose private when resources should only be accessible within your VPCs. Choose public when resources need internet accessibility and global DNS resolution.

Which statement about VPC DNS attributes is correct? A. enableDnsSupport can be true while enableDnsHostnames is false, and DNS resolution will work fully B. enableDnsHostnames can be true while enableDnsSupport is false, and instances will get hostnames C. Both enableDnsSupport and enableDnsHostnames must be true for instances to get public DNS hostnames D. These attributes only affect public DNS resolution, not private hosted zone functionality ✅ C. Both enableDnsSupport and enableDnsHostnames must be true for instances to get public DNS hostnames 🎯 Key insight: enableDnsSupport enables the Amazon DNS server functionality, while enableDnsHostnames determines if instances get public DNS hostnames. Both must be true for full DNS functionality. If enableDnsSupport is false, the Amazon DNS server at 169.254.169.253 won't work, breaking DNS resolution entirely.

A company needs to ensure their internal database servers can be accessed by applications across multiple VPCs using custom domain names , but the databases should never be resolvable from the internet . Which Route 53 feature best addresses this requirement? A. Route 53 Resolver with forwarding rules B. Private hosted zones associated with VPCs C. Public hosted zones with restricted access policies D. Route 53 health checks with failover routing ✅ B. Private hosted zones associated with VPCs 🎯 Perfect match: Private hosted zones provide DNS resolution for custom domain names exclusively within associated VPCs, ensuring internal resources are never resolvable from the internet while enabling cross-VPC access through VPC peering. Resolver forwarding is for hybrid scenarios, public zones would expose to internet, and health checks are for availability monitoring, not DNS isolation.

Requirements: DNS resolution for internal services , cross-VPC accessibility , no internet exposure , custom domain names , integration with existing VPC peering . Which Route 53 configuration meets ALL requirements? A. Public hosted zone with IAM-based access control B. Private hosted zone associated with all relevant VPCs C. Route 53 Resolver endpoints with conditional forwarding D. CloudFront distribution with origin access identity ✅ B. Private hosted zone associated with all relevant VPCs 🎯 Requirement mapping: Private hosted zones provide custom domain DNS (✓), work within VPCs only (✓), support cross-VPC resolution through peering (✓), ensure no internet exposure (✓), and integrate seamlessly with existing VPC infrastructure (✓). Public zones expose to internet, Resolver endpoints are for hybrid connectivity, CloudFront is for content delivery not internal DNS resolution.

A company has multiple AWS accounts for different departments (finance, HR, engineering). Each account has a Systems Administrator with root access . The company needs to centrally manage policies to allow or deny AWS services for individual accounts or groups of accounts. Which is the most suitable solution with the LEAST complexity? A. Connect all departments by setting up cross-account access to each AWS account. Create and attach IAM policies to resources based on departments. B. Use AWS Organizations and Service Control Policies to control the list of AWS services that can be used by each member account. C. Set up AWS Organizations and Organizational Units (OU) to connect all AWS accounts. Create a custom IAM Policy to allow or deny certain AWS services for each account. D. Provide access to externally authenticated users via Identity Federation. Set up an IAM role to specify permissions for users from each department. ✅ B. Use AWS Organizations and Service Control Policies 🎯 Why correct: Service Control Policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations are specifically designed for centrally managing permissions across multiple AWS accounts. Unlike IAM policies which only affect users/groups/roles within an account, SCPs can restrict even the root user and affect all identities in member accounts. ⚠️ A. Cross-account access with IAM policies This approach creates significant complexity with multiple cross-account trust relationships and doesn't provide centralized policy management. Each account would need individual IAM policy configuration, defeating the purpose of centralized control. ⚠️ C. AWS Organizations with custom IAM Policy While AWS Organizations is correct, IAM policies cannot restrict services across accounts or affect the root user. Only Service Control Policies (SCPs) can centrally control AWS service access across multiple accounts in an organization. ⚠️ D. Identity Federation with IAM roles This solution addresses user authentication but doesn't solve the core requirement of centrally managing service permissions across multiple AWS accounts. It focuses on federated access rather than service control.

When should you use Service Control Policies (SCPs) versus IAM policies for access management? A. Use SCPs for single-account resource permissions, IAM policies for multi-account service restrictions B. Use SCPs for multi-account service restrictions, IAM policies for single-account resource permissions C. Use SCPs for temporary access, IAM policies for permanent access D. Use SCPs for external users, IAM policies for internal users ✅ B. Use SCPs for multi-account service restrictions, IAM policies for single-account resource permissions Service Control Policies (SCPs) • Work across multiple AWS accounts in an organization • Can restrict even the root user • Control which AWS services can be used • Applied at OU or account level • Act as guardrails (maximum permissions) IAM Policies • Work within a single AWS account • Cannot restrict the root user • Control access to specific resources and actions • Applied to users, groups, or roles • Grant actual permissions 🎯 Decision rule: Choose SCPs when you need to set boundaries across multiple accounts or restrict services organization-wide. Choose IAM policies when you need to grant specific permissions to identities within an account.

Which statement about AWS Organizations Service Control Policies (SCPs) is correct? A. SCPs grant permissions to users and can override IAM policy denies B. SCPs only apply to IAM users and groups, not roles or the root account C. SCPs act as guardrails and can restrict even the root account identity D. SCPs automatically replace all existing IAM policies in member accounts ✅ C. SCPs act as guardrails and can restrict even the root account identity 🎯 Key insight: SCPs are unique because they can restrict the root account, which IAM policies cannot do. They work as guardrails (maximum permissions) rather than granting permissions. SCPs affect all identities in an account including users, groups, roles, and root. They work alongside IAM policies, not replacing them.

A company wants to prevent any account in their organization from launching expensive EC2 instance types while still allowing individual account administrators to manage their own IAM permissions for other services. Which AWS service best addresses this requirement? A. AWS Config Rules B. AWS Organizations Service Control Policies C. AWS IAM Permission Boundaries D. AWS Systems Manager Compliance ✅ B. AWS Organizations Service Control Policies 🎯 Trigger mapping: The phrase "prevent any account in their organization" signals a need for organization-wide service restrictions that override local account permissions. Only SCPs can restrict services across all accounts while allowing account admins to maintain IAM control for permitted services. Config Rules detect non-compliance but don't prevent actions. Permission Boundaries work within single accounts only. Systems Manager doesn't control EC2 launch permissions.

Requirements: Centrally manage 50+ AWS accounts , enforce security baselines , prevent certain regions from being used , allow account owners to manage their own users , and automate new account creation . Which service combination meets ALL requirements? A. AWS Control Tower with Organizations B. AWS Config with CloudFormation StackSets C. AWS Organizations with Service Control Policies only D. AWS IAM Identity Center with Cross-Account Roles ✅ A. AWS Control Tower with Organizations 🎯 Requirement mapping: Control Tower provides automated account creation, security baselines (guardrails), and region restrictions while using Organizations underneath for account management. It includes SCPs for restrictions while preserving account autonomy for user management. Config + StackSets lacks account creation automation. Organizations alone doesn't provide security baselines or automated setup. Identity Center focuses on SSO, not account governance or region restrictions.

A multinational financial company has web applications in multiple VPCs across various AWS regions . They need a logging solution to track all changes to AWS resources including EC2, S3, CloudFront, and IAM. The solution must ensure security, integrity, and durability of log data for compliance and provide event history of all AWS account activity across management console, SDKs, CLI, and API calls. Which option provides the best solution? A. Create AWS CloudTrail trail with --is-multi-region-trail and --include-global-service-events, encrypt with KMS, enable MFA Delete on S3 bucket B. Create Amazon CloudWatch trail with --include-global-service-events only, encrypt with KMS, enable MFA Delete on S3 bucket C. Create AWS CloudTrail trail with --no-include-global-service-events and --is-multi-region-trail, encrypt with KMS, enable MFA Delete D. Create Amazon CloudWatch trail with --is-multi-region-trail and --include-global-service-events, encrypt with KMS, enable MFA Delete ✅ A. AWS CloudTrail with multi-region and global service events enabled 🎯 Why correct: CloudTrail is the correct service for API call logging. The --is-multi-region-trail captures events across all regions, while --include-global-service-events ensures IAM and CloudFront activities are logged. KMS encryption and MFA Delete provide required security controls. ⚠️ B. CloudWatch trail with incomplete parameters CloudWatch is for metrics and monitoring, not API call logging. Additionally, --is-multi-region-trail is missing, so it won't capture events from all regions where the company operates. ⚠️ C. CloudTrail with global services explicitly disabled The --no-include-global-service-events parameter prevents logging of IAM, CloudFront, and other global services that the scenario specifically mentions needing to track. ⚠️ D. CloudWatch trail (wrong service) CloudWatch is used for metrics, alarms, and logs from applications, not for tracking AWS API calls and resource changes across the account.

When should you choose AWS CloudTrail over Amazon CloudWatch for logging requirements? A. When you need to monitor application performance metrics and set up alarms B. When you need to track API calls and changes to AWS resources for compliance C. When you need to collect and analyze custom application logs from EC2 instances D. When you need real-time streaming of operational data to dashboards ✅ B. When you need to track API calls and changes to AWS resources for compliance AWS CloudTrail • Records API calls made to AWS services • Tracks resource changes and user activity • Provides audit trail for compliance • Covers both regional and global services • Stores events in S3 for long-term retention Amazon CloudWatch • Monitors performance metrics and system health • Collects application and system logs • Sets up alarms and notifications • Creates dashboards for operational visibility • Provides real-time monitoring capabilities 🎯 Decision rule: Choose CloudTrail when you need governance, compliance, and audit trails of who did what. Choose CloudWatch when you need operational monitoring, metrics, and alerting.

Which statement about AWS CloudTrail global service events is correct? A. Global service events are automatically included in all CloudTrail trails by default B. Global service events can only be captured in the us-east-1 region and must be explicitly enabled C. Global service events include EC2 and RDS activities across all regions D. Global service events cannot be encrypted with KMS keys for security ✅ B. Global service events can only be captured in the us-east-1 region and must be explicitly enabled 🎯 Key insight: Global services like IAM, CloudFront, Route 53, and AWS WAF operate from us-east-1. You must use --include-global-service-events to capture these events. EC2 and RDS are regional services, not global. Global service events can be encrypted with KMS just like regional events.

A company needs to track who deleted an S3 bucket and monitor when IAM policies are modified across their multi-region AWS environment for security auditing. Which service best addresses this requirement? A. Amazon CloudWatch Logs with custom log streams B. AWS Config with configuration history tracking C. AWS CloudTrail with multi-region trail and global service events D. Amazon EventBridge with custom event patterns ✅ C. AWS CloudTrail with multi-region trail and global service events 🎯 Why CloudTrail: The trigger phrases "who deleted" and "when policies are modified" indicate the need for API call auditing . CloudTrail captures the identity (who), timestamp (when), and action details. Multi-region captures S3 deletions across regions, while global service events capture IAM policy changes. ⚠️ AWS Config tracks resource configuration changes but doesn't provide the "who" information (user identity) that performed the action.

Requirements: Log retention for 7+ years , tamper-proof audit trail , encrypt all log data , and prevent accidental deletion of historical logs for financial compliance. Which combination of services meets ALL requirements? A. CloudWatch Logs with log retention policies and IAM restrictions B. CloudTrail with S3 bucket, KMS encryption, MFA Delete, and S3 Object Lock C. AWS Config with configuration snapshots stored in encrypted S3 D. CloudTrail with CloudWatch Logs integration and log group retention ✅ B. CloudTrail with S3 bucket, KMS encryption, MFA Delete, and S3 Object Lock 🎯 Requirements mapping: CloudTrail provides audit trail • S3 enables 7+ year retention • KMS encrypts data • MFA Delete prevents accidental deletion • S3 Object Lock ensures tamper-proof storage with WORM (Write Once Read Many) compliance. ⚠️ A. CloudWatch Logs has maximum retention of 10 years but doesn't provide the same tamper-proof guarantees as S3 Object Lock. ⚠️ D. CloudWatch integration doesn't provide the long-term durability and compliance features needed for financial audit requirements.

A telecommunications company is hosting a WordPress website on Amazon ECS Cluster using Fargate launch type . Database credentials must be provided via environment variables , kept secure and not viewable on the cluster. Requirements: dedicated storage with lifecycle management and key rotation . Which solution provides secure credential storage with the least effort? A. Store credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, encrypt with KMS, create IAM role for ECS task execution, reference secrets in container definition B. Migrate to Amazon EKS, use Kubernetes Secrets objects, reference with secretKeyRef, configure automatic rotation C. Store credentials in ECS task definition file encrypted with KMS, store in private S3 bucket with HTTPS, use --cli-input-json parameter D. Store credentials in AWS Secrets Manager, encrypt with KMS, create IAM role for ECS task execution, reference secrets in container definition ✅ D. AWS Secrets Manager with KMS encryption 🎯 Why correct: Secrets Manager provides dedicated secrets storage with built-in lifecycle management and automatic key rotation capabilities, exactly matching the requirement for "dedicated storage with lifecycle management and key rotation." ⚠️ A. Systems Manager Parameter Store While Parameter Store can store encrypted credentials and works with ECS secrets, it doesn't provide dedicated storage with lifecycle management and key rotation features like Secrets Manager does. ⚠️ B. Migrate to Amazon EKS This requires significant migration effort from ECS to EKS, violating the "least effort" requirement. Additionally, Kubernetes doesn't natively support automatic rotation of secrets. ⚠️ C. Store in ECS task definition in S3 Storing sensitive credentials in S3, even encrypted, is not a recommended practice and requires extensive manual configuration. This approach has more overhead than using purpose-built secrets management services.

When should you choose AWS Secrets Manager over Systems Manager Parameter Store for storing database credentials? A. When you need the lowest cost option for storing credentials B. When you need dedicated secrets storage with automatic rotation and lifecycle management C. When you want to store both configuration data and secrets in the same service D. When you need to store large configuration files with secrets ✅ B. When you need dedicated secrets storage with automatic rotation and lifecycle management Secrets Manager • Dedicated secrets management service • Built-in automatic rotation • Lifecycle management features • Higher cost but more features • Best for database credentials, API keys Parameter Store • General configuration management • Lower cost option • No built-in rotation • Stores both config and secrets • Best for application configuration 🎯 Decision rule: Choose Secrets Manager when you need dedicated secrets storage with rotation. Choose Parameter Store when you want a single store for both configuration and secrets at lower cost.

Which statement about ECS secrets injection is correct? A. Secrets can only be referenced from the same AWS region as the ECS task B. Secrets are injected at container startup and stored in the container filesystem C. Secrets can be referenced from different regions but must be from the same AWS account D. ECS secrets injection only works with EC2 launch type, not Fargate ✅ C. Secrets can be referenced from different regions but must be from the same AWS account 🎯 Why correct: ECS allows cross-region secret references within the same account, providing flexibility for multi-region deployments. The secrets are injected as environment variables, not stored in the filesystem, and work with both EC2 and Fargate launch types.

A company needs to automatically rotate database passwords every 30 days for their containerized applications running on ECS. The solution must have built-in rotation capabilities and minimal operational overhead . Which AWS service best addresses this requirement? A. AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store with Lambda rotation B. AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation C. Amazon S3 with KMS encryption and lifecycle policies D. AWS Config with remediation actions ✅ B. AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation 🎯 Built-in rotation: Secrets Manager has native automatic rotation capabilities with pre-built Lambda functions for common databases, requiring minimal setup and operational overhead. ⚠️ A. Parameter Store with Lambda: Requires custom Lambda function development and maintenance, increasing operational overhead.

Requirements: Store database credentials for ECS Fargate tasks, encrypt data at rest , automatic key rotation , lifecycle management , minimal development effort , and dedicated secrets storage . Which service combination meets ALL requirements? A. Parameter Store + KMS + custom Lambda rotation B. Secrets Manager + KMS with automatic rotation C. S3 + KMS + lifecycle policies + custom rotation D. RDS encrypted snapshots + manual rotation ✅ B. Secrets Manager + KMS with automatic rotation 🎯 Perfect match: Secrets Manager provides dedicated secrets storage, built-in lifecycle management, automatic rotation, and KMS encryption. All requirements met with minimal development effort. ⚠️ A. Parameter Store: Requires custom Lambda development for rotation, not dedicated secrets storage. ⚠️ C. S3: Not designed for secrets storage, requires extensive custom development.

A media company has web applications in US West (N. California) behind an Application Load Balancer with public SSL/TLS certificates for HTTPS traffic via FQDNs. The architect must upgrade to a multi-region architecture across regions like ap-southeast-2, ca-central-1, eu-west-3. Which approach ensures all HTTPS services continue working without interruption? A. In each new AWS Region, request SSL/TLS certificates using AWS KMS for each FQDN B. In each new AWS Region, request SSL/TLS certificates using AWS Certificate Manager for each FQDN C. Use AWS KMS in US West to request certificates for all FQDNs to use across all regions D. Use AWS Certificate Manager in US West to request certificates for all FQDNs to use across all regions ✅ B. In each new AWS Region, request SSL/TLS certificates using AWS Certificate Manager for each FQDN 🎯 Why correct: ACM certificates for Application Load Balancers are region-specific . Unlike CloudFront which can use certificates from us-east-1 globally, ALBs require certificates to be requested in the same region where the load balancer is deployed. ⚠️ A. AWS KMS for certificates AWS KMS is for data encryption and key management, not SSL/TLS certificate provisioning. ACM is the correct service for managing SSL certificates that integrate with AWS services like ALB. ⚠️ C. AWS KMS cross-region Double mistake: KMS isn't for certificates, and even if it were, certificates can't be shared across regions for ALBs. Each region needs its own certificate. ⚠️ D. ACM cross-region sharing While ACM is correct, certificates from one region cannot be used by ALBs in other regions. Cross-region certificate sharing only works with CloudFront distributions using us-east-1 certificates.

When should you use ACM certificates with CloudFront versus Application Load Balancer? A. CloudFront requires certificates in us-east-1, ALB requires regional certificates B. CloudFront uses regional certificates, ALB uses us-east-1 certificates C. Both CloudFront and ALB can share certificates across all regions D. Both CloudFront and ALB require certificates in each deployment region ✅ A. CloudFront requires certificates in us-east-1, ALB requires regional certificates CloudFront + ACM • Certificate must be requested in us-east-1 • Single certificate distributed globally • Automatic global distribution • Cost-effective for global CDN ALB + ACM • Certificate must be in same region as ALB • Separate certificate per region • Regional certificate management • Direct load balancer integration 🎯 Decision rule: Use CloudFront approach for global content delivery with single certificate management. Use ALB approach for regional load balancing with region-specific certificates.

Which statement about AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate deployment is correct? A. ACM certificates can be exported and manually installed on any EC2 instance B. ACM certificates automatically renew but only for ACM-integrated AWS services C. ACM certificates work with all AWS services across all regions automatically D. ACM certificates must be manually renewed every 90 days like Let's Encrypt ✅ B. ACM certificates automatically renew but only for ACM-integrated AWS services 🎯 Key insight: ACM provides automatic renewal for certificates deployed to integrated services like ALB, CloudFront, and API Gateway. Certificates cannot be exported for manual installation on EC2 instances - they're managed entirely within AWS integrated services. This automation removes the operational burden of certificate lifecycle management.

A company needs to secure HTTPS connections for web applications deployed across multiple AWS regions using Application Load Balancers . They want automated certificate management without manual renewal processes. Which service best addresses this requirement? A. AWS KMS with custom certificate generation B. AWS Certificate Manager with regional certificates C. Third-party certificate authority with manual deployment D. AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store with certificate storage ✅ B. AWS Certificate Manager with regional certificates 🎯 Trigger mapping: "Multiple regions + ALB + automated management" → ACM regional certificates . ACM provides automatic provisioning, deployment, and renewal for ALB certificates, eliminating manual certificate lifecycle management across regions. ⚠️ A. AWS KMS: KMS is for encryption key management, not SSL certificate provisioning and lifecycle management. ⚠️ C. Third-party CA: Requires manual renewal and deployment processes, contradicting the automation requirement. ⚠️ D. Parameter Store: Only for storing values, doesn't provide certificate generation or automatic renewal capabilities.

A solutions architect proposes using a single ACM certificate from us-west-1 for Application Load Balancers across multiple regions to reduce management overhead. Why is this problematic? A. ACM certificates cannot be shared across regions for ALB deployments B. The certificate will have higher latency in other regions C. Cross-region certificate usage increases costs significantly D. The certificate will not support SNI across regions ✅ A. ACM certificates cannot be shared across regions for ALB deployments This approach fails because ALB requires certificates to be in the same region as the load balancer. Unlike CloudFront which can use us-east-1 certificates globally, ALB has strict regional certificate requirements for security and compliance reasons. 🎯 Better approach: Request separate ACM certificates in each target region where ALBs will be deployed. This ensures proper certificate-to-service binding and maintains security boundaries while still providing automatic renewal benefits.

A company is modernizing its on-premises system by migrating to AWS. The system will be hosted on EC2 instances managed by Amazon EKS and use Amazon RDS for MySQL . The system has predictable schedules of high usage during sales events and holiday seasons. What pricing options should the company consider for the MOST cost-optimized solution? A. EC2 Instance Savings Plans for regular traffic, On-Demand scaling, 1-year Partial Upfront RDS Reserved Instance with vertical scaling B. Standard Reserved Instances for regular traffic, Dedicated Instances for scaling, 1-year All Upfront RDS Reserved Instance C. Compute Savings Plans for regular traffic, On-Demand Capacity Reservations for scaling, 1-year No Upfront RDS Reserved Instance with read replicas D. Compute Savings Plans for regular traffic, Spot instances for scaling, 1-year All Upfront RDS Reserved Instance with vertical scaling ✅ D. Compute Savings Plans for regular traffic, Spot instances for scaling, 1-year All Upfront RDS Reserved Instance with vertical scaling 🎯 Why correct: This combines maximum cost optimization with flexibility: Compute Savings Plans offer up to 66% savings with flexibility across instance families, Spot instances provide up to 90% savings for predictable peak periods, and All Upfront Reserved Instances maximize database cost savings for predictable workloads. ⚠️ A. EC2 Instance Savings Plans + On-Demand scaling EC2 Instance Savings Plans limit flexibility to specific instance families, and On-Demand instances are significantly more expensive than Spot instances for predictable peak traffic. Partial Upfront Reserved Instances also provide less cost savings than All Upfront payment. ⚠️ B. Standard Reserved Instances + Dedicated Instances Standard Reserved Instances offer less flexibility than Savings Plans, and Dedicated Instances are the most expensive EC2 option, typically used for compliance rather than cost optimization during peak traffic periods. ⚠️ C. On-Demand Capacity Reservations + No Upfront RDS On-Demand Capacity Reservations ensure capacity availability but provide zero cost savings compared to Spot instances. No Upfront Reserved Instances offer the smallest discount compared to All Upfront payment for predictable database workloads.

When should you choose Compute Savings Plans over EC2 Instance Savings Plans for cost optimization? A. When you need maximum possible savings and use a single instance family B. When you need flexibility across instance families and services like Fargate and Lambda C. When you want to reserve capacity in specific Availability Zones D. When you need dedicated hardware for compliance requirements ✅ B. When you need flexibility across instance families and services like Fargate and Lambda EC2 Instance Savings Plans • Up to 72% savings (highest) • Specific instance family in region • Limited to EC2 only • Best for stable, predictable workloads Compute Savings Plans • Up to 66% savings • Any instance family, size, OS, tenancy • Covers EC2, Fargate, Lambda • Maximum flexibility across services 🎯 Decision rule: Choose EC2 Instance when you have stable workloads on specific instance families. Choose Compute when you need flexibility across instance types or use multiple compute services.

Which statement about RDS Reserved Instance payment options is correct? A. No Upfront provides the highest discount but requires monthly payments B. Partial Upfront offers better savings than All Upfront with lower risk C. All Upfront provides the maximum discount by paying the entire term in advance D. All payment options provide identical total cost over the reserved term ✅ C. All Upfront provides the maximum discount by paying the entire term in advance 🎯 Payment hierarchy for maximum savings: All Upfront > Partial Upfront > No Upfront. The more you pay upfront, the larger the discount. All Upfront eliminates ongoing monthly charges and provides the best total cost optimization for predictable workloads like the database scenario.

A company has predictable traffic spikes during known events like Black Friday sales that last 2-4 hours. They need to scale EC2 capacity cost-effectively during these periods while maintaining application availability. Which scaling approach best addresses this requirement? A. On-Demand Capacity Reservations B. Spot Instances C. Dedicated Hosts D. Standard Reserved Instances ✅ B. Spot Instances 🎯 Perfect match: Spot instances provide up to 90% cost savings for predictable short-duration workloads. Since the traffic spikes are scheduled and temporary, the risk of interruption is manageable through proper instance diversification and capacity planning. On-Demand Capacity Reservations ensure capacity but provide zero cost savings compared to Spot instances for this predictable use case.

Requirements: Containerized application on Kubernetes , predictable baseline load , scheduled traffic spikes , MySQL database with known usage patterns , maximum cost optimization . Which combination meets ALL requirements? A. EKS with On-Demand instances + RDS with No Upfront Reserved B. ECS with Spot instances + DynamoDB with On-Demand billing C. EKS with Compute Savings Plans baseline + Spot scaling + RDS All Upfront Reserved D. EC2 with Dedicated Hosts + Aurora Serverless ✅ C. EKS with Compute Savings Plans baseline + Spot scaling + RDS All Upfront Reserved 🎯 Requirements mapping: EKS handles Kubernetes requirement, Compute Savings Plans optimize baseline costs with flexibility, Spot instances maximize savings during predictable spikes, RDS MySQL meets database requirement, All Upfront Reserved maximizes database cost savings for known usage patterns. Option B uses ECS instead of Kubernetes and DynamoDB instead of required MySQL database.

A clinic runs its medical record system using Windows-based EC2 instances with confidential health files. Requirements: latest security patches must be installed and there should be a system that checks all EC2 instances for approved AMIs . The solution must not impede developers from launching instances with unapproved AMIs, but you must be notified of non-compliant instances . Which TWO solutions should the architect implement? (Select TWO.) A. Set up a patch baseline using AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager B. Set up Amazon GuardDuty to monitor patches and AMI compliance C. Use AWS Shield Advanced to automatically patch instances D. Create an IAM policy restricting unapproved AMI launches E. Use AWS Config Managed Rule to check approved AMIs with CloudWatch Alarms ✅ A & E. AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager + AWS Config Managed Rule 🎯 Why correct: Patch Manager handles automated patching with customizable baselines, while Config Managed Rules continuously monitor AMI compliance without blocking developer actions. CloudWatch Alarms provide the required notifications for non-compliance. ⚠️ B. Amazon GuardDuty GuardDuty is a threat detection service that monitors for malicious activity and unauthorized behavior. It does not check security patch status or AMI compliance - it focuses on detecting threats like unusual API calls or potential account compromises. ⚠️ C. AWS Shield Advanced Shield Advanced is specifically designed for DDoS protection and mitigation. It has no capabilities for patching EC2 instances or monitoring AMI compliance - it's purely a network-level protection service. ⚠️ D. IAM Policy Restriction While technically possible, creating an IAM policy that blocks unapproved AMI launches would directly violate the requirement that the solution "should not impede developers from launching instances using an unapproved AMI."

When should you choose AWS Config over Amazon GuardDuty for compliance monitoring? A. When you need to detect malicious network activity B. When you need to check resource configuration compliance against rules C. When you need to protect against DDoS attacks D. When you need to analyze DNS logs for threats ✅ B. When you need to check resource configuration compliance against rules AWS Config • Evaluates resource configurations against rules • Tracks configuration changes over time • Provides compliance dashboards • Uses managed rules for common compliance checks • Focuses on configuration drift and compliance Amazon GuardDuty • Detects malicious activity and threats • Monitors network traffic patterns • Analyzes DNS logs and VPC Flow Logs • Uses machine learning for threat detection • Focuses on security incidents and anomalies 🎯 Decision rule: Choose Config when you need to ensure resources meet compliance standards and track configuration changes. Choose GuardDuty when you need to detect active security threats and malicious behavior.

Which statement about AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager is correct? A. It can only patch Windows instances, not Linux instances B. It uses patch baselines to define approved and rejected patches C. It requires custom Lambda functions for all patching operations D. It automatically patches instances without any configuration needed ✅ B. It uses patch baselines to define approved and rejected patches 🎯 Why correct: Patch Manager uses patch baselines as the core mechanism to control which patches are approved for installation. These baselines include rules for auto-approving patches within specified timeframes and explicit lists of approved/rejected patches. Option A is wrong because it supports both Windows and Linux. Option C is wrong because managed rules don't require Lambda functions. Option D is wrong because patch baselines and maintenance windows must be configured.

A company needs to continuously monitor whether EC2 instances comply with approved AMI standards and receive notifications when non-compliant instances are detected, but without preventing developers from launching any instances. Which service best addresses this monitoring requirement? A. Amazon CloudTrail with CloudWatch Events B. AWS Config with managed rules C. AWS Systems Manager Compliance D. Amazon Inspector with assessment templates ✅ B. AWS Config with managed rules 🎯 Perfect match: AWS Config provides managed rules specifically for checking EC2 AMI compliance (like approved-amis-by-id ). It continuously evaluates resources against rules and can trigger CloudWatch Alarms for notifications without blocking any actions. ⚠️ A. CloudTrail: Logs API calls but doesn't evaluate compliance against rules ⚠️ C. Systems Manager Compliance: Focuses on patch compliance, not AMI compliance ⚠️ D. Inspector: Performs security assessments of applications, not AMI compliance checks

A solutions architect proposes using IAM policies to prevent developers from launching EC2 instances with unapproved AMIs to ensure compliance. Why is this problematic for the clinic scenario? A. IAM policies cannot control AMI selection during instance launch B. It violates the requirement to not impede developer workflows C. IAM policies are too expensive for this use case D. It would require modifying every existing EC2 instance ✅ B. It violates the requirement to not impede developer workflows The scenario explicitly states that "the system should not impede developers from launching instances using an unapproved AMI." Using restrictive IAM policies would directly prevent developers from launching unapproved AMIs, which contradicts this key requirement. The goal is monitoring and notification, not prevention. 🎯 Better approach: Use AWS Config rules for continuous compliance monitoring with CloudWatch Alarms for notifications. This allows detection and alerting without blocking developer actions, meeting both the compliance and workflow requirements.

A company with 50 research teams across multiple facilities needs a multi-account AWS strategy. Each team requires its own AWS account, but there's only one DNS management team handling all domains and subdomains for the organization. The solution must allow private DNS sharing among VPCs in different AWS accounts with the least complex DNS architecture. Which solution provides the simplest DNS architecture while allowing all VPCs to resolve needed domain names? A. Set up VPC peering among all VPCs. Create Route 53 private hosted zone in central account. Create private hosted zones in each other account with Name Server entries pointing to central account. B. Use AWS RAM to set up shared services VPC in central account. Set up VPC peering from shared VPC to each account's VPC. Create Route 53 private hosted zone associated with shared VPC. Programmatically associate other VPCs with this hosted zone. C. Use AWS RAM to set up shared services VPC in central account. Create VPC peering to each account's VPC. Create Route 53 private hosted zone in shared VPC. Create private hosted zones in each other account with Name Server entries pointing to central account. D. Set up Direct Connect connections among VPCs with private virtual interfaces. Set enableDnsHostnames and enableDnsSupport to FALSE. Create Route 53 private hosted zone in central account. Programmatically associate other VPCs with this hosted zone. ✅ B. Use AWS RAM with shared services VPC and programmatic VPC association to Route 53 hosted zone 🎯 Why correct: This approach uses AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) to create a centralized shared services VPC that can be peered with all other account VPCs. The key differentiator is programmatically associating VPCs from other accounts with the hosted zone , which allows direct DNS resolution without complex NS record configurations. ⚠️ A. VPC peering with NS record configuration While VPC peering connects the networks properly, configuring Name Server entries in each account's Route 53 zones to point to the central account won't work for private hosted zone resolution. Route 53 private hosted zones require VPC association , not NS record redirection. ⚠️ C. Shared VPC with NS record configuration Although the shared services VPC approach is sound, this option still relies on configuring NS records in each account to point to the central DNS, which doesn't work for private hosted zones. You need direct VPC association with the hosted zone, not NS record forwarding. ⚠️ D. Direct Connect with DNS attributes disabled Direct Connect is designed for on-premises connectivity, not inter-VPC communication within AWS. Additionally, setting enableDnsHostnames and enableDnsSupport to FALSE would disable VPC DNS resolution , preventing resources from querying Route 53 zones at all.

Which statement about Route 53 private hosted zones in multi-account environments is correct? A. Private hosted zones can be shared across accounts by configuring Name Server (NS) records in each account to point to the zone owner's DNS servers. B. VPCs from different accounts can resolve private hosted zone records only if they are programmatically associated with the hosted zone. C. Private hosted zones automatically inherit DNS resolution capabilities when VPCs are connected via VPC peering or Transit Gateway. D. Cross-account private hosted zone access requires Direct Connect or VPN connections between the accounts. ✅ B. VPCs from different accounts require programmatic association with the hosted zone 🎯 Why correct: Route 53 private hosted zones work through VPC association , not network connectivity alone. Even if VPCs are connected via peering or transit gateway, cross-account VPCs must be explicitly associated with the private hosted zone to resolve its records. NS record forwarding doesn't work for private zones, and network connectivity methods don't automatically grant DNS resolution access.

When should you use AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) VPC sharing versus individual VPCs with Transit Gateway for multi-account network architecture? A. Use RAM VPC sharing when you need centralized network control and shared infrastructure; use Transit Gateway when accounts need network isolation with selective connectivity. B. Use Transit Gateway for all multi-account scenarios as it provides better security; RAM VPC sharing should only be used within single accounts. C. Use RAM VPC sharing for temporary connections; use Transit Gateway for permanent multi-account networking. D. Both services provide identical functionality; choose based on cost preferences only. ✅ A. RAM VPC sharing for centralized control and shared infrastructure; Transit Gateway for network isolation with selective connectivity AWS RAM VPC Sharing • Centralized VPC management and control • Shared subnets across accounts • Cost optimization through shared NAT gateways, VPC endpoints • Higher subnet density • Participants reference each other's security groups • Best for: Organizations wanting centralized network ops AWS Transit Gateway • Each account maintains own VPCs • Selective routing and connectivity control • Network segmentation and isolation • Scalable hub-and-spoke model • Route table controls for traffic flow • Best for: Accounts needing network autonomy with controlled interconnection 🎯 Decision rule: Choose RAM VPC sharing when you want centralized network operations, shared infrastructure costs, and don't need strict network boundaries between accounts. Choose Transit Gateway when accounts need to maintain their own network boundaries but require selective, controlled connectivity between them.

A company has 50 development teams across multiple regions, each requiring their own AWS account for isolation. However, they want to minimize networking complexity and share common services like DNS, NAT gateways, and VPC endpoints across all teams while maintaining centralized network control . Which service best addresses this requirement? A. AWS Transit Gateway with shared route tables B. AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) with VPC sharing C. AWS PrivateLink with cross-account endpoint sharing D. VPC Peering with centralized routing ✅ B. AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) with VPC sharing 🎯 The trigger phrases "minimize networking complexity," "share common services," and "centralized network control" directly map to RAM VPC sharing capabilities. This allows one account to own and manage the VPC while sharing subnets with other accounts, enabling shared infrastructure like NAT gateways and VPC endpoints while maintaining central control. ⚠️ A. Transit Gateway: Provides connectivity but each account still maintains separate VPCs, requiring duplicate NAT gateways and endpoints - doesn't minimize complexity or enable infrastructure sharing. ⚠️ C. PrivateLink: Only shares specific services via endpoints, doesn't provide comprehensive network sharing or centralized control of routing and infrastructure. ⚠️ D. VPC Peering: Creates point-to-point connections but doesn't enable infrastructure sharing or centralized management - actually increases complexity with 50 accounts.

Requirements: Cross-account private DNS resolution , single DNS management team , 50+ AWS accounts , minimal operational overhead , and least complex architecture . Which combination of services meets ALL requirements? A. VPC Peering + Route 53 Resolver forwarding rules + multiple private hosted zones B. Transit Gateway + Route 53 Resolver endpoints + shared Route 53 private hosted zone C. AWS RAM VPC sharing + Route 53 private hosted zone + programmatic VPC association D. Direct Connect + Route 53 public hosted zones + VPC DNS forwarding ✅ C. AWS RAM VPC sharing + Route 53 private hosted zone + programmatic VPC association 🎯 Requirements mapping: Cross-account DNS: VPC association enables this. Single management team: One central hosted zone. 50+ accounts: RAM scales efficiently. Minimal overhead: No per-account zone management. Least complex: Single shared VPC hub with spoke connections rather than mesh topology. ⚠️ A. Requires managing multiple zones and complex forwarding rules across 50 accounts - high overhead. ⚠️ B. Resolver endpoints add complexity and cost; doesn't leverage VPC sharing benefits. ⚠️ D. Direct Connect is for on-premises, public zones don't provide private resolution.

A startup is building a web app for users to post photos of good deeds with 143-character captions . The developers chose ReactJS to run on the broadest range of browsers and mobile devices. The app needs access to Amazon DynamoDB to store captions. Initial prototype shows no large usage spikes . Which option provides the most cost-effective and scalable architecture for this application? A. Configure ReactJS client with temporary credentials from STS using a Token Vending Machine (TVM) on EC2. Serve from S3 bucket enabled as website. B. Register with Web Identity Provider (Google, Facebook, Amazon) and use AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity API. Create IAM role for GET/PUT operations in S3 and DynamoDB. Serve from S3 bucket enabled as website. C. Register with Web Identity Provider and create IAM role for DynamoDB access. Serve from NGINX on EC2 instances with load balancer and auto-scaling. D. Configure ReactJS client with TVM credentials for DynamoDB access. Serve from NGINX on load-balanced, auto-scaled EC2 instances with IAM role. ✅ B. Web Identity Provider with AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity API, S3 static website hosting 🎯 Why correct: ReactJS applications are essentially static files that render dynamically in the browser. S3 static website hosting is the most cost-effective solution, while Web Identity Providers offer secure, scalable authentication without managing infrastructure. AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity provides proper temporary credentials for AWS service access. ⚠️ A. Token Vending Machine on single EC2 Creates a single point of failure since the TVM runs on just one EC2 instance. This architecture is neither highly available nor fault-tolerant, and the single instance becomes a performance bottleneck as usage grows. ⚠️ C. Web Identity Provider with EC2/NGINX While using Web Identity Providers is correct, serving from EC2 instances with load balancers is significantly more expensive than S3 static hosting. The startup requirement emphasizes cost-effectiveness, making this unnecessarily complex and costly. ⚠️ D. TVM with EC2/NGINX infrastructure Combines the worst of both worlds: expensive EC2 infrastructure when S3 would suffice, plus the TVM approach without mentioning Security Token Service for temporary credential generation. More costly and complex than needed.

When should you choose S3 static website hosting over EC2 with load balancers for a ReactJS application? A. When the application requires server-side processing and dynamic content generation B. When cost-effectiveness is a priority and the app consists of static files rendered client-side C. When the application needs to maintain server state and session information D. When complex load balancing algorithms and health checks are required ✅ B. When cost-effectiveness is a priority and the app consists of static files rendered client-side S3 Static Website Hosting • Extremely cost-effective (pay for storage + requests only) • Perfect for ReactJS/client-side rendered apps • Built-in high availability and durability • No server maintenance required • Scales automatically EC2 with Load Balancer • Required for server-side processing • More expensive (EC2 + ELB costs) • Better control over infrastructure • Supports complex routing and health checks • Requires maintenance and patching 🎯 Decision rule: Choose S3 when you have client-side rendered apps (ReactJS, Angular, Vue) that don't need server-side processing. Choose EC2 when you need server-side logic, APIs, or backend processing.

Which statement about AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity API is correct? A. It requires an EC2 instance to act as a Token Vending Machine for credential distribution B. It exchanges authentication tokens from web identity providers for temporary AWS credentials C. It can only be used with Amazon Cognito and cannot work with external identity providers D. It provides permanent IAM user credentials for web applications to access AWS services ✅ B. It exchanges authentication tokens from web identity providers for temporary AWS credentials 🎯 Key insight: AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity is an STS API that allows applications to trade authentication tokens from external identity providers (Google, Facebook, Amazon, etc.) for temporary AWS credentials. This eliminates the need to store permanent AWS credentials in client applications and provides secure, time-limited access to AWS resources. It works with any OIDC-compatible identity provider, not just Cognito.

A solutions architect proposes using a Token Vending Machine (TVM) on a single EC2 instance to provide credentials for a ReactJS web application. Why is this problematic? A. TVM cannot generate temporary credentials for web applications B. Single EC2 instance creates a single point of failure and performance bottleneck C. ReactJS applications cannot consume credentials from a TVM service D. TVM requires integration with Amazon Cognito which adds unnecessary complexity ✅ B. Single EC2 instance creates a single point of failure and performance bottleneck The Token Vending Machine approach using a single EC2 instance introduces critical reliability issues. If the EC2 instance fails, the entire authentication system becomes unavailable, making the architecture neither fault-tolerant nor highly available. Additionally, as user traffic increases, the single instance becomes a performance bottleneck since all credential requests must flow through it. 🎯 Better approach: Use Web Identity Federation with AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity API, which eliminates infrastructure dependencies and provides built-in scalability and availability through AWS STS service.

A company is building a client-side JavaScript application that needs to authenticate users through social media accounts and allow them to upload files directly to S3 and write data to DynamoDB tables without exposing AWS credentials in the browser. Which AWS service best addresses this authentication requirement? A. AWS IAM Users with embedded access keys in the JavaScript code B. Amazon Cognito User Pools with Web Identity Federation C. AWS Lambda functions acting as authentication proxies D. Amazon API Gateway with custom authorizers ✅ B. Amazon Cognito User Pools with Web Identity Federation 🎯 Trigger mapping: The combination of client-side JavaScript + social media authentication + direct AWS service access + no embedded credentials directly points to Cognito with Web Identity Federation. This provides secure temporary credentials through STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity without exposing permanent AWS credentials in browser code. ⚠️ A. Embedding access keys in JavaScript exposes credentials to anyone who views the source code - a major security vulnerability. ⚠️ C. Lambda proxies add unnecessary complexity and latency when direct service access is possible with proper authentication. ⚠️ D. API Gateway with custom authorizers doesn't directly solve the social media authentication requirement and adds infrastructure overhead.

A company needs to migrate an Oracle database to PostgreSQL in AWS. This is a heterogeneous migration requiring schema and code transformation before data migration can begin. Which approach is most suitable for this database migration? A. Use AWS SAM to transform database to PostgreSQL using Lambda functions, then migrate with DMS B. Use AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) to convert source schema, then migrate data using DMS to RDS PostgreSQL C. Use AWS Application Migration Service, then use DMS to convert and migrate to RDS PostgreSQL D. Use AWS Glue to convert schema and code, then use AWS Batch with Spot instances for data migration ✅ B. Use AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) to convert source schema, then migrate data using DMS to RDS PostgreSQL 🎯 Why correct: Heterogeneous migrations require a two-step process: first convert schema/code with AWS SCT , then migrate data with AWS DMS . SCT is specifically designed for Oracle-to-PostgreSQL conversions. ⚠️ A. AWS SAM + Lambda approach AWS SAM is for building serverless applications, not database schema conversion. Lambda functions are not designed for complex Oracle-to-PostgreSQL schema transformations that require understanding database-specific syntax and data types. ⚠️ C. AWS Application Migration Service Application Migration Service migrates entire applications and infrastructure, not individual databases. While DMS is correct for data migration, this skips the critical schema conversion step that SCT provides. ⚠️ D. AWS Glue + Batch approach AWS Glue is an ETL service for data preparation and analytics, not for Oracle-to-PostgreSQL schema conversion. AWS Batch with Spot instances doesn't handle the database-specific migration complexities that DMS manages.

When should you use AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) versus AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) alone? A. Use SCT alone for all database migrations to ensure schema compatibility B. Use DMS alone for both homogeneous and heterogeneous migrations C. Use SCT first for heterogeneous migrations, then DMS for data migration D. Use SCT and DMS simultaneously for faster migration performance ✅ C. Use SCT first for heterogeneous migrations, then DMS for data migration AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) • Converts database schemas and code • Handles Oracle to PostgreSQL transformations • Converts stored procedures, functions, views • Provides assessment reports • Required for heterogeneous migrations AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) • Migrates actual data between databases • Supports homogeneous migrations alone • Maintains source database availability • Handles ongoing replication • Performs automatic data type conversions 🎯 Decision rule: Use SCT when database engines differ (Oracle→PostgreSQL), then DMS for data. Use DMS alone when engines are the same (Oracle→Oracle).

Which statement about heterogeneous database migrations is correct? A. AWS DMS automatically handles all schema conversions during migration B. Heterogeneous migrations require a two-step process: schema conversion then data migration C. AWS Glue is the primary service for converting Oracle schemas to PostgreSQL D. Schema differences between database engines don't affect migration complexity ✅ B. Heterogeneous migrations require a two-step process: schema conversion then data migration 🎯 Why correct: When database engines differ (Oracle vs PostgreSQL), schema structures, data types, and database code can be quite different. AWS SCT must first convert schemas and code, then AWS DMS migrates the actual data. This two-step approach ensures compatibility between different database platforms.

A company needs to migrate from SQL Server stored procedures to MySQL functions while preserving business logic during database migration. Which service best addresses this requirement? A. AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) B. AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) C. AWS Glue DataBrew D. Amazon RDS Performance Insights ✅ B. AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) 🎯 Key trigger: When you need to convert database code (stored procedures, functions, triggers) between different database engines, SCT is the specialized tool. It understands database-specific syntax and automatically converts business logic. ⚠️ A. DMS only migrates data, not stored procedures or functions ⚠️ C. Glue DataBrew is for data preparation and cleansing, not code conversion ⚠️ D. Performance Insights monitors database performance, doesn't convert code

Requirements: Migrate Oracle database to PostgreSQL with minimal downtime , preserve all stored procedures , and maintain data consistency during migration. Which combination of services meets ALL requirements? A. AWS Application Migration Service + RDS B. AWS SCT + DMS + RDS PostgreSQL C. AWS Glue + Lambda + RDS PostgreSQL D. AWS DataSync + EC2 + PostgreSQL ✅ B. AWS SCT + DMS + RDS PostgreSQL 🎯 Requirements mapping: • Preserve stored procedures: SCT converts Oracle PL/SQL to PostgreSQL functions • Minimal downtime: DMS keeps source database operational during migration • Data consistency: DMS handles ongoing replication and validation • Target platform: RDS PostgreSQL provides managed database service

A tech company's smartwatch will collect user statistics. The solution must ingest millions of records per minute globally. Requirements: records , durable storage , 120-day retention , low latency retrieval , 10-15 TB yearly . Which storage solution is most cost-effective? A. Amazon MSK to ingest and store records with 120-day retention, plus S3 for durability B. S3 buckets with unique filenames per record and lifecycle policy for 120-day expiration C. DynamoDB table with proper scaling and TTL setting for 120-day deletion D. Aurora Serverless with Lambda function to delete records older than 120 days ✅ C. DynamoDB table with proper scaling and TTL setting for 120-day deletion 🎯 Why correct: DynamoDB TTL automatically deletes expired items without consuming write throughput, making it cost-effective. Provides low-latency retrieval and handles millions of writes per minute with proper scaling. ⚠️ A. Amazon MSK + S3 MSK is not optimized for low-latency data retrieval - it's designed for streaming. The additional S3 storage adds unnecessary cost and complexity for this use case. ⚠️ B. S3 with unique filenames S3 doesn't provide low-latency retrieval for millions of small objects. Each record becomes a separate S3 object, creating inefficient storage patterns and higher retrieval times. ⚠️ D. Aurora Serverless + Lambda With constant data ingestion, Aurora Serverless won't provide cost benefits as the database will always be active. Manual deletion via Lambda consumes additional compute resources.

Which statement about DynamoDB TTL is correct? A. TTL deletion consumes write capacity units from your table B. TTL automatically deletes items without consuming write throughput C. TTL requires a scheduled Lambda function to perform deletions D. TTL can only delete items that are exactly 120 days old ✅ B. TTL automatically deletes items without consuming write throughput 🎯 DynamoDB TTL is a background process that automatically removes expired items at no additional cost and without consuming any write capacity units. You simply define a timestamp attribute, and DynamoDB handles the rest. Options A and C are incorrect because TTL doesn't require manual intervention or consume WCUs. Option D is wrong because TTL works with any timestamp value, not fixed periods.

When should you choose DynamoDB over S3 for storing millions of small records? A. When you need the cheapest possible storage costs B. When you need low-latency retrieval and frequent access patterns C. When records are larger than 400KB each D. When you only need to store data for archival purposes ✅ B. When you need low-latency retrieval and frequent access patterns DynamoDB • Single-digit millisecond latency • Optimized for frequent reads/writes • Built-in scaling for high throughput • TTL for automatic cleanup S3 • Lower cost per GB stored • Optimized for larger objects • Higher latency for small objects • Lifecycle policies for transitions 🎯 Decision rule: Choose DynamoDB when you need fast access to frequently queried small records. Choose S3 when cost optimization and archival are priorities over access speed.

A company needs to automatically delete data after a specific retention period without manual intervention or consuming additional resources. Which AWS feature best addresses this requirement? A. S3 Lifecycle Policies B. DynamoDB TTL C. Lambda scheduled functions D. RDS automated backups ✅ B. DynamoDB TTL 🎯 The key trigger phrase is "without consuming additional resources" . DynamoDB TTL is the only option that deletes data automatically without consuming write capacity units or requiring manual scheduling. S3 Lifecycle works for object transitions but isn't for active database records. Lambda functions consume compute resources. RDS backups don't delete production data.

Requirements: Millions of writes per minute , records under 4KB , low-latency reads , automatic 120-day cleanup , cost-effective scaling Which storage service meets ALL requirements? A. Amazon S3 with lifecycle policies B. Amazon RDS with scheduled cleanup C. DynamoDB with TTL D. Amazon Redshift with automatic vacuum ✅ C. DynamoDB with TTL 🎯 Requirement mapping: Millions of writes → DynamoDB auto-scaling ; Small records → optimized for ; Low-latency reads → single-digit millisecond response ; 120-day cleanup → TTL automatic deletion ; Cost-effective → no additional cleanup costs ⚠️ A. S3: High latency for small object retrieval, not optimized for millions of writes per minute ⚠️ B. RDS: Requires manual cleanup scripts, not optimized for this write volume ⚠️ D. Redshift: OLAP system, not designed for high-frequency transactional writes

A private bank hosts a secure web application for agents to view highly sensitive client information . The CISO requires that the SSL private key cannot be moved outside the corporate environment . Application logs may contain sensitive data and must be stored securely and durably , accessible only to authorized employees. EBS volumes are encrypted and traffic levels are known and stable . Which architecture meets all security and availability requirements? A. ELB with TCP load balancing, AWS CloudHSM for SSL, private S3 with server-side encryption for logs B. ELB with TCP load balancing, SSL private key retrieved from S3 on boot, S3 server-side encryption for logs C. ELB with SSL offloading, encrypted instance store for logs using random AES key D. ELB with TCP load balancing, CloudHSM in two AZs for SSL, private S3 with server-side encryption for logs ✅ D. ELB with TCP load balancing, CloudHSM in two AZs for SSL, private S3 with server-side encryption for logs 🎯 Why correct: CloudHSM ensures SSL private keys stay in AWS hardware security modules and cannot be extracted. Deploying across two AZs provides high availability. S3 with SSE-C allows customer-managed encryption keys for authorized employee access only. ⚠️ A. Single AZ CloudHSM While CloudHSM secures the SSL key, deploying to only one AZ creates a single point of failure, violating the high availability requirement for a critical banking application. ⚠️ B. S3 key retrieval Storing SSL private keys in S3 allows them to be downloaded and potentially moved outside the corporate environment, directly violating the CISO's key security requirement. ⚠️ C. Instance store logs Instance store volumes are ephemeral - data is lost when EC2 instances terminate. This violates the durability requirement for application logs that must be retained for compliance.

When should you choose AWS CloudHSM over AWS Certificate Manager for SSL certificate management? A. When you need automatic certificate renewal B. When you need the private key to remain in dedicated hardware that cannot be extracted C. When you want the lowest cost solution D. When you need integration with CloudFront ✅ B. When you need the private key to remain in dedicated hardware that cannot be extracted AWS CloudHSM • Hardware security module you control • Private keys never leave HSM hardware • FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated • Custom key management policies • Higher cost, more control AWS Certificate Manager • Fully managed certificate service • Automatic renewal and deployment • Free for AWS services • AWS manages private keys • Easier to use, less control 🎯 Decision rule: Choose CloudHSM when regulatory compliance requires hardware-based key isolation and you need full control over cryptographic operations. Choose ACM when you want managed certificates with automatic renewal for standard SSL/TLS use cases.

Which statement about S3 Server-Side Encryption with Customer-Provided Keys (SSE-C) is correct? A. AWS stores your encryption keys and manages key rotation automatically B. Amazon S3 stores a salted HMAC of your key but not the actual key C. Encryption keys are stored in AWS KMS for backup and recovery D. S3 can decrypt objects even if you lose the original encryption key ✅ B. Amazon S3 stores a salted HMAC of your key but not the actual key 🎯 Key insight: With SSE-C, you provide the encryption key with each request. S3 uses it to encrypt/decrypt your data, then removes the key from memory. Only a salted HMAC hash is stored for validation - this cannot be used to derive the original key or decrypt data. If you lose your key, you lose access to your data permanently.

A financial services company needs to ensure that cryptographic keys for SSL certificates cannot be extracted or moved outside their AWS environment due to regulatory compliance requirements. Which AWS service best addresses this requirement? A. AWS Key Management Service (KMS) B. AWS CloudHSM C. AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) D. AWS Secrets Manager ✅ B. AWS CloudHSM 🎯 Why CloudHSM: Provides dedicated hardware security modules where cryptographic operations occur entirely within the HSM hardware. Private keys are generated and stored in the HSM and cannot be extracted in plaintext , meeting strict regulatory requirements for key isolation. ⚠️ KMS: AWS manages the underlying hardware - keys could theoretically be accessed by AWS ⚠️ ACM: AWS fully manages certificates and private keys ⚠️ Secrets Manager: Stores secrets that can be retrieved by applications

Requirements: High availability for critical banking app, durable log storage accessible only to authorized users, stable traffic patterns , and SSL termination without key extraction risk . Which combination meets ALL requirements? A. Single AZ CloudHSM + S3 with SSE-S3 B. Multi-AZ CloudHSM + S3 with SSE-C C. Application Load Balancer with SSL termination + CloudWatch Logs D. Network Load Balancer + EC2 with SSL + EBS encrypted storage ✅ B. Multi-AZ CloudHSM + S3 with SSE-C 🎯 Requirements mapping: • High availability: Multi-AZ CloudHSM eliminates single points of failure • Durable storage: S3 provides 11 9's durability • Authorized access only: SSE-C allows customer-managed encryption keys • No key extraction: CloudHSM keeps keys in dedicated hardware • Stable traffic: TCP load balancing works well for predictable patterns

A multi-tier web application uses an Application Load Balancer and EC2 instances across three Availability Zones. During peak load, stateless web servers operate at 95% utilization . Current architecture uses Reserved Instances for steady-state load and On-Demand Instances for peak load. The system needs improvement for cost-effectiveness and quick recovery when an AZ becomes unavailable during peak load. Which architecture provides the most cost-effective solution for AZ failure recovery during peak load? A. Use a combination of Spot and On-Demand instances on each AZ to handle both steady state and peak load B. Use a combination of Reserved and On-Demand instances on each AZ to handle both steady state and peak load C. Launch an Auto Scaling group of Reserved instances on each AZ to handle peak load. Retain current setup for steady state D. Launch a Spot Fleet using diversified allocation strategy, with Auto Scaling enabled on each AZ for peak load. Retain current setup for steady state ✅ D.
